citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed oriented smooth surface with positive area form $\eta$ and an orientation-compatible complex structure $j$. Use its smooth complex symmetric product $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$, $m\ge1$, and the descended product symplectic form $\omega$ off the diagonal. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m$ be disjoint embedded circles, and likewise $\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_m$, with every alpha-beta intersection transverse. Let $T_\alpha,T_\beta\subset X$ be their product tori. Fix finitely many points $p$ of $\Sigma$ away from all these circles and the associated divisors $E_p=\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}\Sigma$.

The intersection $K=T_\alpha\cap T_\beta$ is finite and disjoint from the diagonal and all $E_p$. There exist pairwise disjoint neighborhoods $U_x$ of its points, with closures disjoint from those protected sets, and smooth coordinate charts $q_x$ centered at $x$ taking $T_\alpha,T_\beta$ to $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$. There is a smooth almost complex structure $J_*$ on $X$ equal to $\operatorname{Sym}^m(j)$ near the diagonal and all $E_p$, taming $\omega$ elsewhere, and exactly $i$ in each $q_x$ chart near $x$.

More generally any smooth family $J_t$ with the first two properties can be modified inside the $U_x$, retaining its values outside them and near all protected sets, to have those exact product-integrable values on smaller neighborhoods for every $t$. The constant path $J_*$ therefore provides a genuine admissible geometric choice with the local hypotheses needed for product-integrable end asymptotics. No regularity or moduli count is asserted for that path.

Assume countable choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed diagram for one oriented knot in $S^3$, with the complete compression disks, simultaneously parallel knot arcs and cyclic ordered marks of the pointed-data convention. Its individual cut-surface components are $A_i,B_i$, with $w_i,z_i\in A_i$ and $w_i,z_{i+1}\in B_i$ for $1\le i\le k$, cyclically. Fix its surface complex structure, area form, target metric, a region point in each region, and product generator charts avoiding the diagonal and all chosen region and marked divisors. Consider actual smooth finite-energy holomorphic strips with uniform generator ends, for nearly symmetric paths integrable near those divisors and the diagonal, satisfying $n_{z_i}(u)=0$ for every $i$. The $w_i$ multiplicities may be positive.

For every ordered generator pair there is one fixed nonnegative integer $S_{xy}$ such that every such strip with those ends satisfies $\sum_i n_{w_i}(u)=S_{xy}$. Only finitely many actual integral region domains occur for that pair. For each possible $w$-multiplicity vector there is at most one such domain. Every same-generator strip in this class is constant. The energies of all these strips, across all generator pairs and all actual indices and Whitney classes, have one finite upper bound.

The finite-domain conclusions hold simultaneously for paths with the fixed geometric data. The energy conclusion holds simultaneously whenever their domain-energy constants have one common bound, in particular on a sufficiently small $C^0$ neighborhood with the integrable neighborhoods and generator charts fixed. In the case that a pair admits no strip, take $S_{xy}=0$ and its domain set empty. This supplies a finiteness and energy prerequisite for the zero-$z$ knot Floer differential with positive $w$ powers; it asserts no regularity, square-zero, grading formula, move invariance or grid-to-analytic comparison.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix compact transverse strip data with finite generator set $K=L_0\cap L_1$, and a smooth background path $J_t^b$ constant on endpoint collars, with fixed totally real boundary structures and exact all-$t$ charts taking the two boundaries to $\mathbb R^m,i\mathbb R^m$ and $J_t^b$ to $i$. Choose pairwise disjoint compact neighborhoods $A_x$ of the generators inside those charts and a compact set $D$ disjoint from their union. Choose smaller working generator charts with closures inside $\operatorname{Int}(A_x)$. All references to preserved exact generator charts below mean these smaller working charts; the original larger background charts remain available to analyze a strip whose entire image lies in $A_x$. Put $P_X=D\cup\bigcup_xA_x$, and require all desired spatially protected values on $P_X$. For an optional tameness requirement, assume the closure of $X\setminus P_X$ is a compact subset of an open region carrying the specified smooth two-form and that $J^b$ tames that form there.

There is an actual separable Hilbert ball of smooth paths $J_t(a)$ preserving the protected spatial values, generator charts, boundary structures and optional tameness, such that every derivative of $J(a)-J^b$ at $t=0,1$ vanishes. Finite parameter tangent combinations are dense in every finite coefficient norm in the smooth anti-$J(a)$ fields compactly supported in $(0,1)\times(X\setminus P_X)$. The actual universal strip section is a submersion at every nonconstant finite-energy strip, including those with the same end generator. A dense residual set of parameters makes all these actual strip linearizations surjective in $H^1\to L^2$ and in every integer higher Hilbert Sobolev realization simultaneously.

These auxiliary paths are not asserted to be constant on any endpoint collar. Every one is, however, a smooth coefficient limit of paths $J^{(\epsilon)}$ which are constant on genuine endpoint collars, have the same protected spatial and boundary values and exact generator charts, and retain tameness. No regularity of those approximating paths is asserted here. Transferring regularity to them requires a separate compactness and operator argument; a limit of shrinking collars is not treated as an admissible fixed-collar path.

Assume Countable Choice and the nearly symmetric marked strip geometry of the zero-marked bubble-exclusion lemma. In particular all individual boundary curve-system complement components contain marked points, and the almost complex paths have common exact product generator charts, common protected diagonal/region/marked-divisor neighborhoods, and fixed totally real boundary structures. Let $J^*$ be a smooth path in this geometry such that every nonconstant finite-energy zero-marked $J^*$ strip has surjective actual $H^1\to L^2$ linearization. It need not be constant on time-endpoint collars. Fix $E_0<\infty$.

Suppose $J_n\to J^*$ smoothly, with those same fixed geometric structures, including the common generator charts, and uniform nearly symmetric energy constants. Then for all sufficiently large $n$, every zero-marked $J_n$ strip of energy at most $E_0$ has surjective actual linearization. In fact specified right inverses $L^2\to H^1$ can be chosen with one uniform finite bound for all these strips and all sufficiently large $n$, using a fixed smooth target connection flat in the generator charts. Surjectivity also holds in every integer higher Hilbert Sobolev realization.

Consequently a generic auxiliary flat-endpoint-jet path supplied by the flat-jet universal regularity theorem has genuine constant-collar approximating paths which are regular for all zero-marked strips of energy at most this fixed $E_0$. This supplies bounded-energy constant-collar regularity, including same-generator strips. It does not supply a uniform energy bound for all Floer classes of a prescribed index; any such admissibility/domain-index argument remains a separate prerequisite for unrestricted moduli counts or index-two compactifications.

Assume Countable Choice and the complete marked nearly symmetric geometry, protected neighborhoods and exact product generator charts of the zero-marked bubble-exclusion lemma. Fix $E_0<\infty$, end generators $x_-,x_+$, and an actual smooth path $J_t$ for which every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most $E_0$ has surjective actual linearization. Such a path with genuine endpoint collars is supplied by the bounded-energy collar-openness lemma.

There are finitely many longitudinal-translation orbits of nonconstant zero-marked $J_t$ strips from $x_-$ to $x_+$ with energy at most $E_0$ and real Fredholm index one. This remains true simultaneously over the finite set of ordered end pairs. Their counts modulo two are therefore well-defined integers modulo two. The index is the actual $H^1\to L^2$ operator index, before translation quotient. No identification with a separately named Maslov or domain index is asserted, and the theorem supplies no energy bound for an unrestricted collection of Floer classes.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix the compact nearly symmetric Heegaard geometry with complete marked cut systems, protected diagonal and region-divisor neighborhoods, and common exact product generator charts used in zero-marked bubble exclusion. Every complement component of each individual boundary curve system must contain a marked point. Whitney classes mean continuous two-marked disk relative-homotopy classes with the two boundary arcs on the specified product tori. Their integer $\mu$ is the actual fixed-end Fredholm index constructed by continuous relative smoothing, not a domain Euler formula.

Fix a class $\phi:x\to z$ with $\mu(\phi)=2$ and with all marked divisor degrees zero. Its region divisor degrees $n_R(\phi)$ are well-defined integers. For a common domain-energy constant $C$ put
$$B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta.$$
Choose a smooth path with genuine constant endpoint collars, the stipulated protected data, and actual regularity for every nonconstant zero-marked strip of energy at most a number $E_0>B_\phi$. Such paths exist by the auxiliary flat-jet regularity and actual bounded-energy collar-approximation theorems, with $C$ taken uniform in the approximating neighborhood as proved below.

For this path, the moduli space $\widehat{\mathcal M}(\phi)$ of actual strips in $\phi$ modulo longitudinal translation is a Hausdorff second-countable topological one-manifold. It has a compactification by finitely many boundary points. These points are exactly the ordered pairs of actual index-one strip orbits
$$([u],[v]),\qquad u:x\to y,\quad v:y\to z,\quad [u]*[v]=\phi.$$
Each such component has zero marked degrees and energy at most $B_\phi$. Each boundary point has the actual one-sided gluing collar with smooth interior from the regular-pair collar theorem. No differentiability at a prescribed compactifying parameter is asserted.

The number of these boundary points is even. Equivalently the sum modulo two of the products of rigid counts over the factorizations $\phi=\phi_1*\phi_2$ with $\mu(\phi_1)=\mu(\phi_2)=1$ is zero; only finitely many factors with nonzero counts occur. This is the cancellation identity for this fixed zero-marked class. It does not establish finiteness over all classes of prescribed index, a domain-index formula, positive-marked boundary-degeneration cancellation, or polygon/target-degeneration gluing.

Assume countable choice. Retain the compact target, totally real boundary submanifolds, fixed path $J_t$ and exact product generator charts of the smooth relative-homotopy index lemma. A continuous Whitney representative from $x$ to $y$ is a continuous disk map with two specified boundary points mapped to $x,y$ and its two boundary arcs mapped into $L_0,L_1$. Equivalence means an actual continuous relative homotopy fixing those points and preserving the two boundary conditions.

Every such class has a smooth fixed-end strip representative, constant on full tails. If two smooth fixed-end representatives are continuously relatively homotopic, there is a smooth relative homotopy between them with one common pair of constant tails and the same fixed endpoints. Consequently the quotient of smooth fixed-end representatives by those smooth homotopies identifies with the continuous Whitney-class set. The actual real Fredholm index of its fixed-end Cauchy–Riemann-symbol linearization therefore defines an integer $\mu(\phi)$ on every continuous Whitney class; it agrees with the actual index of each smooth fixed-end model, is additive under class concatenation, is zero on the constant class, and changes sign under reversal.

For an actual smooth finite-energy holomorphic strip with uniform generator ends, its actual Fredholm index equals this index of its continuously compactified Whitney class.

This proves a continuous-class index using genuine representatives and relative homotopies. It does not identify that integer with a domain Euler measure, corner multiplicities or a first-Chern pairing; no nonlinear moduli counts or their regularity are asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. In the compact transverse geometry with common exact product generator charts, let an actual sequence of strips have the unbubbled breaking conclusion of the strip compactness theorem, with nonconstant levels $v_1,\ldots,v_M$, matched end generators and no additional energy or image diameter on the intermediate necks or outer tails. Each strip determines its continuous Whitney class by filling its two uniform generator ends, with boundary arcs on $L_0,L_1$. Concatenation joins matching constant end neighborhoods, or equivalently the corresponding marked disk ends.

For all sufficiently large $n$, the actual relative classes satisfy
$$[u_n]=[v_1]*\cdots*[v_M].$$
These are classes under continuous homotopies fixing the two marked ends and preserving each boundary arc. The conclusion uses the actual image collapse and smooth core convergence, not just equality of divisor degrees or energy. It applies in particular to the actual zero-marked unbubbled compactness conclusion, without any additional index hypothesis.

For the actual regular-pair pregluing $u_R$ and Newton-corrected strip $g_R$ in the regular-strip gluing lemma, for all sufficiently large $R$ one has
$$[g_R]=[u_R]=[u^-]*[u^+].$$
No converse classification of relative classes, Maslov/domain formula, or gluing for bubbles or degenerating targets is asserted.

derivations.claim: If $m=0$, then $h=0,k=1$, the symmetric product is a point, and the generator set consists of its one point. Its only strip is constant and has index zero on the zero-dimensional section space. Therefore $\partial_z=0$ and the conclusion is direct. Suppose $m>0$. Apply [F1] to obtain a background with exact generator charts avoiding the finitely many protected divisors and diagonal. Choose separated smaller compact generator neighborhoods and a protected compact neighborhood of those divisors and diagonal. They satisfy the separated spatial-set hypotheses in [F2]; the free spatial closure lies away from the diagonal, where the descended product form is smooth. Take a small coefficient neighborhood with all these protected data fixed, small enough that one constant $C$ works in the domain-energy estimate by [F1]. The finite set $\mathcal D$ of actual zero-$z$ domains supplied there works for every path under consideration. Define $$G=1+\max\left(\{0\}\cup\left\{C\sum_R n_R(D)\int_R\eta:D\in\mathcal D\right\}\right).$$ Actual region coefficients are nonnegative. Hence every actual zero-$z$ strip has energy less than $G$, regardless of index or class. This is a bound for the entire domain set, not a bound imposed by deleting classes. Empty actual domain sets use $G=1$. [F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

Choose an auxiliary all-strip regular path in that neighborhood using [F2], and apply its actual collar-approximation theorem at threshold $E_0=3G$. A sufficiently close approximant is a smooth genuine constant-collar path with the same protected geometry and common $C$, regular for every nonconstant zero-$z$ strip of energy at most $3G$. Fix this ONE path for the remainder of the proof. Every strip used below is for this same path. By [F3] and step1.1, its index-one translation quotient is finite across all classes and generator pairs. All such strips are nonconstant: a constant generator strip has the constant-class index zero by [F4], agreeing with its actual transverse constant operator. The finite counts in the Statement are therefore precisely these regular rigid orbits, and their nonnegative integral $w$ multiplicities give the stated finite polynomial formula. Extend it linearly over the polynomial ring. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, construct]

Fix generators $x,z$. The coefficient of $z$ in $\partial_z^2x$ is a finite sum over ordered pairs of rigid orbits $u:x\to y$, $v:y\to z$ and their intermediate generator $y$, with weight $$U^{\mathbf n_w(u)+\mathbf n_w(v)}.$$ Group these finitely many pairs by the actual continuous concatenated Whitney class $\phi=[u]*[v]$. By [F4] its index is two, and by the divisor-degree additivity in [F3] it has $n_{z_i}(\phi)=0$ and $n_R(\phi)=n_R(u)+n_R(v)\ge0$. Its class bound from [F3] satisfies $$B_\phi=C\sum_R|n_R(\phi)|\int_R\eta\le2(G-1)<3G.$$ The estimate uses the actual domains of the two rigid components, both in $\mathcal D$, and the common $C$; it does not require any formal domain to have a holomorphic representative. Thus the SAME fixed path chosen in step2.1 meets the regularity hypothesis of the fixed-class theorem for every class in this finite grouping. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

Apply [F3] to each such class. Its compactification has boundary exactly all ordered rigid pairs of that concatenated class. Each component of any such pair has nonnegative marked degrees, so zero total $z$ degrees force both components to be zero-$z$. Every pair in that boundary is consequently among the pairs in step3.1; none was omitted by the grouping. Conversely each grouped pair occurs as an actual boundary point by the gluing and exhaustion assertion in [F3]. Their number is even. All pairs of this class have exactly the SAME monomial weight $U^{\mathbf n_w(\phi)}$ by marked-degree additivity. Their total contribution over $\mathbb F_2$ is therefore zero. Summing over the finite class grouping proves that the coefficient of $z$ in $\partial_z^2x$ is zero. This applies to every $x,z$, hence $\partial_z^2=0$ on the free polynomial module. [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

All choices and sums in this argument are justified by the actual geometric, analytic and class suppliers: a single path is selected, every rigid orbit set is finite, and every class grouping is finite. In particular there is no infinite formal sum of per-class cancellation identities, no assumption of a domain-index formula, and no replacement of the full filtered all-$z$ differential by this zero-$z$ operator. The result is the stated count complex with positive $w$ powers permitted; the further grading, invariance and comparison assertions listed outside its scope remain separate obligations. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

boundaries.reason: The Statement assumes one knot and k>=1; empty generator and domain sets are allowed by step 1.1.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 treats m=0 directly; step 4.1 proves zero square over F2.
Step 2.1 selects ONE genuine-collar path for every class and pair; step 1.1 treats the one-point symmetric product.

boundaries.reason: The Statement requires transverse geometric data and the chosen path is regular below the actual global energy threshold.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 groups by actual endpoints and concatenated classes; step 4.1 checks every boundary pair and its weight.
Step 2.1 uses proved CC universal regularity and collar approximation; every subsequent orbit and class grouping is finite.

boundaries.reason: This is existence and square-zero, not an equivalence.
No converse or invariant comparison is asserted.
